meta.title: Mind the elves: why Iceland's roads sometimes take the long way round
meta.deck: In a country of volcanoes and hot springs, some building projects are slowed by creatures nobody has ever seen.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

sents.en: Mind the elves: why Iceland's roads sometimes take the long way round
sents.zh: 当心精灵：冰岛的路为什么有时要绕远
notes: Mind ...：当心……，英式说法，伦敦地铁的 Mind the gap（小心站台间隙）就是这个用法。
take the long way round：绕远路。round 是英式，美式常说 around。
冒号后面是正文要回答的问题，标题常这样先抛出悬念。

sents.en: In a country of volcanoes and hot springs, some building projects are slowed by creatures nobody has ever seen.
sents.zh: 在这个遍布火山和温泉的国家，有些建筑工程被一种谁也没见过的生物拖慢了进度。
notes: a country of volcanoes and hot springs：of 后面说明这个国家的特点。
are slowed by：被……拖慢，被动语态。
creatures nobody has ever seen：nobody has ever seen 修饰 creatures，省略了 that。

sents.en: The reasons say less about magic than about how Icelanders treat their land.
sents.zh: 这背后的原因，与其说和魔法有关，不如说反映了冰岛人怎样对待自己的土地。
notes: say less about A than about B：与其说说明 A，不如说说明 B。
how Icelanders treat their land 是名词性从句，作 about 的宾语。

sents.en: Picture a road crew on the edge of Reykjavik, ready to blast through a field of mossy lava.
sents.zh: 想象一支修路队站在雷克雅未克的边上，准备炸开一片长满青苔的熔岩地。
notes: Picture ...：想象一下……，picture 作动词，用祈使句开头把读者带进场景。
crew：一起干活的一队人，road crew 是修路队。
on the edge of：在……的边上。blast through：用炸药炸开（一条路）。

sents.en: Before the first charge is set, a group of protesters turns up and asks them to stop.
sents.zh: 第一包炸药还没装好，一群抗议者就来了，要求他们停工。
notes: charge 在这里是“一次装填的炸药”，set a charge = 装好炸药。
Before ... is set：时间状语从句用一般现在时，整段用现在时讲故事，更有画面感。
turn up：（突然）出现、到场。

sents.en: Their worry is not the view or the birds, but a large rock that, according to local lore, is home to hidden people.
sents.zh: 他们担心的不是风景，也不是鸟，而是一块大石头：按当地的传说，那里住着“隐身人”。
notes: not A but B：不是 A，而是 B。
that ... is home to hidden people 是定语从句，中间插入了 according to local lore。
lore：民间流传的说法、传说。be home to：是……的家、栖息着……。

sents.en: Stories of the huldufólk, or hidden folk, have been passed down in Iceland for centuries.
sents.zh: 关于“huldufólk”，也就是“隐身人”的故事，在冰岛已经流传了几百年。
notes: huldufólk 是冰岛语，字面意思是“隐藏的人”，后面的 or hidden folk 是英文解释。
folk：人们（较老的说法）。
pass down：（一代一代）往下传，这里用现在完成时被动语态。

sents.en: They are said to look much like humans, to live inside rocks and hills, and to take offence when their homes are disturbed.
sents.zh: 据说他们长得和人很像，住在岩石和山丘里，家被打扰时会生气。
notes: be said to do：据说……。后面三个不定式并列：to look, to live, to take。
take offence：生气、被冒犯，英式拼写 offence，美式是 offense。
disturb：打扰、搅动。

sents.en: Few Icelanders will swear that elves exist, yet surprisingly few will rule it out.
sents.zh: 很少有冰岛人敢打包票说精灵存在，可出人意料的是，也很少有人会断然排除这种可能。
notes: Few ... yet surprisingly few ...：前后两个 few 对照，句子很巧。few = 很少（几乎没有）。
swear：发誓、打包票。
rule it out：排除这种可能，it 指 elves exist 这件事。

sents.en: Asked in surveys, many prefer a cautious shrug: better safe than sorry.
sents.zh: 在调查中被问到时，很多人选择谨慎地耸耸肩：宁可信其有。
notes: Asked in surveys 是过去分词短语，相当于 When they are asked in surveys。
a cautious shrug：谨慎的一耸肩，表示“说不好”。
better safe than sorry：俗语，“小心总比后悔好”，这里译作“宁可信其有”。

sents.en: Over the years, that caution has shaped real decisions.
sents.zh: 这些年来，这份谨慎实实在在地影响了一些决定。
notes: over the years：这些年来，常配现在完成时。
caution：小心、谨慎，cautious 的名词。
shape：塑造、影响。

sents.en: Roads have been rerouted to spare elf rocks, and builders have occasionally hired mediators who claim to negotiate with the hidden residents.
sents.zh: 有些路为了避开“精灵石”而改了路线；建筑商偶尔还会请来自称能和隐身居民谈判的“调解人”。
notes: reroute：改道、改变路线。re- 表示“重新”。
spare：使免受（伤害）、放过。to spare elf rocks = 为了不动精灵石。
occasionally：偶尔。mediator：调解人。claim to do：声称能……。

sents.en: When machines break down or workers fall ill on a site, someone usually jokes that the elves are behind it, and only half of them are joking.
sents.zh: 工地上机器出故障、工人生病时，总有人开玩笑说是精灵在捣鬼，而说这话的人里，只有一半是在开玩笑。
notes: break down：（机器）出故障；fall ill：生病（英式常用）。
be behind sth：是……的幕后原因、在背后搞鬼。
only half of them are joking：只有一半是开玩笑，言下之意是另一半是认真的。

sents.en: In one well-known case, a boulder was lifted out of a road's path and set down a safe distance away, by agreement with all sides.
sents.zh: 在一个很有名的例子里，经过各方同意，一块巨石被从道路要经过的地方吊起，挪到一个安全的距离外放下。
notes: well-known：有名的。
boulder：巨石、大圆石。
lifted out of ... and set down ...：两个过去分词并列，被动语态。
by agreement：经过（各方）同意。all sides：各方。

sents.en: Sceptics roll their eyes at such stories.
sents.zh: 怀疑论者对这类故事只会翻白眼。
notes: sceptic：怀疑论者，英式拼写；美式是 skeptic。
roll one's eyes at：对……翻白眼，表示不屑或不耐烦。

sents.en: But the elves often serve as a stand-in for something easier to defend: a deep respect for the landscape.
sents.zh: 可精灵常常是一种替身，代表着更容易站得住脚的东西：对这片土地风貌的深深敬重。
notes: serve as：充当、起……作用。
stand-in：替身、代替的人或物。
something easier to defend：更容易辩护的东西，冒号后解释是什么。landscape：风景、地貌。

sents.en: Iceland's lava fields took thousands of years to form, and once bulldozed they cannot be put back.
sents.zh: 冰岛的熔岩地花了几千年才形成，一旦被推土机推平，就再也恢复不了。
notes: took thousands of years to form：it takes + 时间 + to do 的变体，主语换成了 lava fields。
once bulldozed：一旦被推平，相当于 once they are bulldozed。
put back：放回原处、恢复原样。

sents.en: Protesters who invoke the hidden folk are often the same people who campaign for nature reserves.
sents.zh: 搬出“隐身人”来抗议的人，往往也就是那些为建立自然保护区奔走的人。
notes: invoke：援引、搬出（某种说法或权威来支持自己）。
campaign for：为……开展运动、奔走呼吁。
nature reserve：自然保护区。两个 who 从句分别修饰 Protesters 和 people。

sents.en: Tourism has given the legends a second life.
sents.zh: 旅游业让这些传说焕发了第二次生命。
notes: give sth a second life：让……重获新生、换一种方式继续存在。
legend：传说。

sents.en: Visitors can take guided walks through “elf gardens”, buy maps of known dwellings and even stay in hotels that keep a small house outside for their invisible neighbours.
sents.zh: 游客可以跟着导游逛“精灵花园”，买标出“已知住处”的地图，甚至住进那些在门外专门给隐形邻居留了一座小房子的酒店。
notes: guided walk：有导游带的步行游览。
dwelling：住处、住所，比较正式。
that keep a small house outside ... 是定语从句，修饰 hotels。

sents.en: Locals are happy to play along, partly because it brings in money and also because they enjoy the joke.
sents.zh: 当地人很乐意配合，一部分是因为能赚钱，也因为他们自己也觉得好玩。
notes: play along：（明知是游戏或玩笑也）配合、顺着演。
partly because ... and also because ...：部分是因为……，也是因为……。
bring in money：带来收入。

sents.en: Whether or not anyone believes in them, the hidden folk do a useful job.
sents.zh: 不管有没有人相信他们，这些隐身人都做了一件有用的事。
notes: whether or not：不管是否……，引导让步状语从句。
believe in：相信……的存在；信任。和 believe（相信某话是真的）不同。

sents.en: They remind a fast-growing country to pause before it digs, and to ask what might be lost.
sents.zh: 他们提醒这个快速发展的国家：动工之前先停一停，问问可能会失去什么。
notes: remind sb to do：提醒某人做某事。后面两个不定式并列：to pause, to ask。
fast-growing：快速发展的，复合形容词。
what might be lost：可能失去的东西，宾语从句。

sents.en: Plenty of places could do with a few elves of their own.
sents.zh: 很多地方也真该有几个自己的精灵。
notes: plenty of：很多（前面学过）。
could do with：（口语）很需要、要是有……就好了。
of their own：属于自己的。

vocab.note: 英式常用祈使句：Mind the step!（小心台阶！）、Mind your head.（小心碰头）。另一个常见意思是“介意”：Do you mind ...?

ex.en: [[Mind]] the step on your way out.
ex.zh: 出去的时候当心台阶。

ex.en: [[Mind]] your head, the ceiling is low.
ex.zh: 小心碰头，天花板很低。

vocab.note: 也说 go the long way round / around。比喻“用麻烦的办法做事”也可以：He always does things the long way round.

ex.en: The bridge was closed, so we took [[the long way round]].
ex.zh: 桥封了，我们只好绕远路。

ex.en: She walks [[the long way round]] to avoid the busy road.
ex.zh: 她宁可绕远走，避开那条车多的路。

vocab.note: crew 指一起工作的一群人：a film crew（摄制组）、a cabin crew（机组乘务员）。作集体名词，英式可以接复数动词。

ex.en: A [[crew]] of six worked through the night to fix the pipe.
ex.zh: 六个人的队伍连夜抢修水管。

ex.en: The film [[crew]] arrived early to set up the lights.
ex.zh: 摄制组一早就来布置灯光。

vocab.note: 可以说地点：on the edge of town（在城边上）；也可以比喻快要发生某事：on the edge of tears（快要哭出来）。

ex.en: They live [[on the edge of]] a forest.
ex.zh: 他们住在一片森林的边上。

ex.en: The company is [[on the edge of]] collapse.
ex.zh: 这家公司已经濒临倒闭。

vocab.note: blast 是爆炸、用炸药炸。blast through 也可以比喻“势不可挡地冲过”：The team blasted through the first round.

ex.en: Engineers had to [[blast through]] the mountain to build the tunnel.
ex.zh: 工程师得炸开山体才能修隧道。

ex.en: The river [[blasted through]] the old wall after the storm.
ex.zh: 暴风雨过后，河水冲垮了那堵老墙。

vocab.note: turn up 常带“没预料到”的意味：He turned up late.（他很晚才来）。也有“调大（音量）”的意思：turn up the music。

ex.en: Only five people [[turned up]] for the meeting.
ex.zh: 只有五个人来开会。

ex.en: My lost keys [[turned up]] in the washing machine.
ex.zh: 我丢的钥匙在洗衣机里找到了。

vocab.note: 不可数名词，常和别的词连用：local lore（当地传说）、folklore（民间传说）、sea lore（航海的老经验）。

ex.en: According to local [[lore]], the lake has no bottom.
ex.zh: 按当地的说法，那个湖深不见底。

ex.en: Grandma knows a lot of old kitchen [[lore]].
ex.zh: 奶奶懂很多厨房里的老窍门。

vocab.note: 常用被动：be passed down from generation to generation（一代代传下来）。也说 hand down。

ex.en: This recipe has been [[passed down]] in our family for years.
ex.zh: 这个菜谱在我们家传了很多年。

ex.en: He [[passed down]] his love of music to his children.
ex.zh: 他把对音乐的热爱传给了孩子们。

vocab.note: take offence at sth：因……而不高兴。英式 offence，美式 offense。No offence, but ...（无意冒犯，不过……）很常用。

ex.en: She [[took offence]] at his joke about her cooking.
ex.zh: 他拿她的厨艺开玩笑，她不高兴了。

ex.en: Please don't [[take offence]]; I was only teasing.
ex.zh: 别生气，我只是开玩笑。

vocab.note: Do not disturb.（请勿打扰）。也可以指弄乱东西：Don't disturb the papers on my desk.

ex.en: Sorry to [[disturb]] you, but your car is blocking mine.
ex.zh: 抱歉打扰，你的车挡住我的车了。

ex.en: The birds were [[disturbed]] by the noise.
ex.zh: 鸟儿被噪音惊扰了。

vocab.note: swear (that) ...：发誓说……。另一个意思是“说脏话”：Don't swear in front of the kids. 过去式 swore，过去分词 sworn。

ex.en: I [[swear]] I locked the door.
ex.zh: 我发誓我锁门了。

ex.en: He [[swore]] he had never seen her before.
ex.zh: 他发誓以前从没见过她。

vocab.note: rule out sth / rule sth out：认为某事不可能、把它排除。Police have not ruled out murder.（警方没有排除谋杀的可能。）

ex.en: Doctors have [[ruled out]] a broken bone.
ex.zh: 医生已经排除了骨折的可能。

ex.en: We can't [[rule out]] more rain this weekend.
ex.zh: 这个周末再下雨的可能不能排除。

vocab.zh: 耸肩（表示不知道或无所谓）
vocab.note: 可作动词也可作名词：He shrugged. / He gave a shrug. shrug sth off = 对……不在乎、不当回事。

ex.en: When I asked where she was, he just [[shrugged]].
ex.zh: 我问她去哪儿了，他只是耸了耸肩。

ex.en: She answered with a [[shrug]] and a smile.
ex.zh: 她耸耸肩，笑了笑，算是回答。

vocab.zh: 小心总比后悔好、宁可谨慎
vocab.note: 常用的俗语，可以单独成句：Take an umbrella—better safe than sorry.

ex.en: Take a jacket. [[Better safe than sorry]].
ex.zh: 带件外套吧，小心总比后悔好。

ex.en: I checked the oven twice; [[better safe than sorry]].
ex.zh: 我检查了两遍烤箱，小心点没错。

vocab.note: be cautious about sth：对……很谨慎。名词 caution（小心），副词 cautiously。

ex.en: Be [[cautious]] when you drive in the snow.
ex.zh: 雪天开车要小心。

ex.en: She is [[cautious]] about lending money to friends.
ex.zh: 她借钱给朋友很谨慎。

vocab.note: shape 作动词，指对事情的发展有决定性影响：Her childhood shaped her views.（童年经历塑造了她的观点。）

ex.en: Books I read as a child [[shaped]] the way I think.
ex.zh: 小时候读的书影响了我思考的方式。

ex.en: Weather [[shapes]] the way people dress.
ex.zh: 天气影响人们的穿着。

vocab.note: re-（重新）+ route（路线）。航班、交通、电话都可以 reroute。

ex.en: Traffic was [[rerouted]] because of the marathon.
ex.zh: 因为马拉松，交通改道了。

ex.en: Our flight was [[rerouted]] to another airport.
ex.zh: 我们的航班改飞了另一个机场。

vocab.zh: 使免受（伤害）；饶过；抽出（时间）
vocab.note: spare sb/sth：让……免受损失。另一个常用意思是“抽出”：Can you spare five minutes?

ex.en: The fire [[spared]] the old church.
ex.zh: 大火没有烧到那座老教堂。

ex.en: Can you [[spare]] a few minutes to help me?
ex.zh: 你能抽几分钟帮我一下吗？

vocab.note: 比 sometimes 更少一些。形容词 occasional：an occasional visitor（偶尔来的客人）。

ex.en: We [[occasionally]] eat out on Fridays.
ex.zh: 我们偶尔周五出去吃饭。

ex.en: He [[occasionally]] forgets his keys.
ex.zh: 他偶尔会忘带钥匙。

vocab.note: 动词 mediate（调解），名词 mediation（调解）。常指在争执双方之间帮忙谈判的人。

ex.en: A [[mediator]] helped the two sides reach a deal.
ex.zh: 一位调解人帮双方达成了协议。

ex.en: Teachers often act as [[mediators]] in playground fights.
ex.zh: 操场上吵架时，老师常充当调解人。

vocab.note: The car broke down on the motorway.（车在高速上抛锚了。）说人时是情绪崩溃：She broke down in tears. 名词 breakdown。

ex.en: Our car [[broke down]] in the middle of nowhere.
ex.zh: 我们的车在荒郊野外抛锚了。

ex.en: The printer [[breaks down]] every Monday.
ex.zh: 打印机每周一都坏。

vocab.note: fall + 形容词表示进入某种状态：fall ill, fall asleep, fall silent。fall ill 比 get sick 正式一点，英式常用。

ex.en: He [[fell ill]] the day before the exam.
ex.zh: 他考试前一天病倒了。

ex.en: Many children [[fall ill]] in winter.
ex.zh: 很多孩子冬天会生病。

vocab.zh: 是……的幕后原因、在背后操纵
vocab.note: Who is behind this? = 这是谁干的？/ 谁在背后指使？

ex.en: Police think a local gang [[is behind]] the thefts.
ex.zh: 警方认为这几起盗窃是当地一个团伙干的。

ex.en: I wonder who [[was behind]] the prank.
ex.zh: 我想知道这个恶作剧是谁干的。

vocab.note: 比 rock、stone 更大，一般指自然形成、表面圆滑的大石头。bouldering 是不用绳索的抱石攀岩。

ex.en: A huge [[boulder]] rolled onto the road.
ex.zh: 一块巨石滚到了路上。

ex.en: The children climbed onto a [[boulder]] by the river.
ex.zh: 孩子们爬上了河边的一块大石头。

vocab.note: by mutual agreement：经双方同意。动词 agree，名词 agreement（协议、同意）。

ex.en: The meeting was moved to Friday [[by agreement]].
ex.zh: 经大家同意，会议改到了周五。

ex.en: They ended the contract [[by mutual agreement]].
ex.zh: 双方协商一致，终止了合同。

vocab.note: 英式 sceptic，美式 skeptic。形容词 sceptical：I'm sceptical about it.（我对此表示怀疑。）

ex.en: Even the [[sceptics]] were impressed by the result.
ex.zh: 连怀疑的人都对结果印象深刻。

ex.en: I was a [[sceptic]] until I tried it myself.
ex.zh: 我自己试过之前一直不信。

vocab.zh: 翻白眼（表示不屑、不耐烦）
vocab.note: roll one's eyes at sb/sth。一个很生动的动作描写，常见于口语和小说。

ex.en: She [[rolled her eyes]] when he told the same joke again.
ex.zh: 他又讲那个笑话时，她翻了个白眼。

ex.en: Teenagers often [[roll their eyes]] at their parents.
ex.zh: 青少年常对父母翻白眼。

vocab.note: 名词，带连字符。电影里的替身演员也叫 stand-in。动词短语 stand in for sb = 代替某人。

ex.en: The teacher was ill, so a [[stand-in]] took the class.
ex.zh: 老师病了，由代课老师来上课。

ex.en: Who will [[stand in for]] you while you're away?
ex.zh: 你不在的时候谁来替你？

vocab.note: 指一大片自然或人造的地形景色：a rural landscape（乡村风光）。也可以比喻：the political landscape（政治格局）。

ex.en: The [[landscape]] here is flat and green.
ex.zh: 这里的地貌平坦，一片绿色。

ex.en: She paints mountain [[landscapes]].
ex.zh: 她画山水风景。

vocab.zh: 用推土机推平；强行推进
vocab.note: bulldozer 是推土机。比喻用法：bulldoze a plan through（强行通过一个计划）。

ex.en: The old cinema was [[bulldozed]] to make way for flats.
ex.zh: 老电影院被推平，给公寓楼腾地方。

ex.en: They want to [[bulldoze]] the park and build a car park.
ex.zh: 他们想推平公园，修个停车场。

vocab.note: Put it back when you've finished.（用完放回去。）也有“推迟”的意思：The meeting was put back a week.

ex.en: Please [[put back]] the books when you're done.
ex.zh: 看完请把书放回原处。

ex.en: Once a forest is gone, it's hard to [[put back]].
ex.zh: 森林一旦没了，就很难恢复。

vocab.zh: 援引、搬出（某种说法来支持自己）
vocab.note: invoke a law / a name / a memory：援引法律、搬出某人的名字、唤起回忆。比较正式。

ex.en: He [[invoked]] his right to remain silent.
ex.zh: 他援引了自己保持沉默的权利。

ex.en: Politicians often [[invoke]] history to win support.
ex.zh: 政客常常搬出历史来争取支持。

vocab.note: campaign 作动词：campaign for / against sth。作名词：an election campaign（竞选活动）。

ex.en: Parents [[campaigned for]] a safer crossing near the school.
ex.zh: 家长们奔走呼吁在学校附近修一条更安全的人行横道。

ex.en: She has spent years [[campaigning for]] clean water.
ex.zh: 她多年来一直为干净的饮用水奔走。

vocab.note: reserve 是“保留地”。a wildlife reserve 野生动物保护区。

ex.en: We saw seals at the [[nature reserve]].
ex.zh: 我们在自然保护区看到了海豹。

ex.en: The marsh became a [[nature reserve]] in 1990.
ex.zh: 这片沼泽在 1990 年成了自然保护区。

vocab.note: give sth a second life：让旧东西换个用途继续用，或让被遗忘的东西重新流行。

ex.en: The old factory got [[a second life]] as an art centre.
ex.zh: 老工厂改成了艺术中心，重获新生。

ex.en: Repair cafés give broken toasters [[a second life]].
ex.zh: 修理咖啡馆让坏了的烤面包机重新派上用场。

vocab.note: 比 home、house 正式，常用于书面或法律、历史语境：ancient cave dwellings（古代穴居）。动词 dwell（居住；老想着）。

ex.en: The village has about 200 [[dwellings]].
ex.zh: 这个村子大约有两百处住房。

ex.en: Archaeologists found an ancient [[dwelling]] under the field.
ex.zh: 考古学家在田地下发现了一处古代住所。

vocab.zh: 配合、顺着（玩笑或游戏）演下去
vocab.note: play along with sb/sth。常指明知不是真的，也装作配合。

ex.en: The kids said they were pirates, so I [[played along]].
ex.zh: 孩子们说自己是海盗，我就顺着演了。

ex.en: He didn't believe her story but decided to [[play along]].
ex.zh: 他不信她的话，但决定先配合着。

vocab.note: partly = in part，部分地。常成对出现：partly because ..., partly because ...。

ex.en: I stayed home, [[partly because]] it was raining.
ex.zh: 我待在家里，一部分原因是在下雨。

ex.en: The trip was cheap, [[partly because]] we camped.
ex.zh: 这次旅行很便宜，部分原因是我们露营。

vocab.note: bring in money / customers / tourists。另一个意思是引进新规定：bring in a new law。

ex.en: The summer festival [[brings in]] thousands of visitors.
ex.zh: 夏季节日吸引来成千上万的游客。

ex.en: Her café [[brings in]] enough to pay the rent.
ex.zh: 她的咖啡馆赚的钱够付房租。

vocab.note: 可以放在句首或句中：I'll go whether or not you come. 也可以拆开：whether you come or not。

ex.en: [[Whether or not]] it rains, the match will go ahead.
ex.zh: 不管下不下雨，比赛照常进行。

ex.en: You have to pay [[whether or not]] you use it.
ex.zh: 不管用不用，你都得付钱。

vocab.note: believe in ghosts（相信有鬼）、believe in yourself（相信自己）。believe sb 是“相信某人说的话”，意思不同。

ex.en: Do you [[believe in]] ghosts?
ex.zh: 你相信有鬼吗？

ex.en: My coach always [[believed in]] me.
ex.zh: 我的教练一直相信我。

vocab.note: 英式口语：I could do with a coffee.（我真想来杯咖啡。）比 need 更委婉、更自然。

ex.en: I [[could do with]] a cup of tea.
ex.zh: 我真想来杯茶。

ex.en: This room [[could do with]] a good clean.
ex.zh: 这房间该好好打扫一下了。

vocab.zh: 精灵（民间传说里的小精怪）
vocab.note: 北欧民间传说里住在石头、山丘里的小精灵。注意复数不规则：elf → elves（像 shelf → shelves、wolf → wolves）。冰岛人也叫它们 huldufólk（隐身人）。形容词 elfin（小巧可爱的）。

ex.en: In the story, three [[elves]] help a poor shoemaker at night.
ex.zh: 故事里，三个小精灵晚上帮一个穷鞋匠干活。

ex.en: Some Icelanders believe an [[elf]] lives in the big rock behind the school.
ex.zh: 有些冰岛人相信学校后面那块大石头里住着一个精灵。

vocab.expr: say less about A than about B
vocab.conn: 主语（事物）+ say(s) less about A + than about B
vocab.zh: 与其说反映了A，不如说反映了B
vocab.note: say 在这里不是“说话”，而是“说明、反映”：这件事 says a lot about 你（很能说明你的为人）。say less about A than about B = 它反映 A 的少，反映 B 的多 → 重点其实在 B。反过来 say more about A than about B 就是重点在 A。主语常是事物：the reasons / the choice / the result。

ex.en: His messy desk [[says less about]] laziness than about how busy he is.
ex.zh: 他桌子乱，与其说是因为懒，不如说是因为太忙。

ex.en: The film's success [[says less about]] the story than about its famous cast.
ex.zh: 这部电影的成功，与其说是因为故事，不如说是因为卡司有名。

ex.en: Where people live often [[says less about]] their taste than about house prices.
ex.zh: 人们住在哪里，与其说取决于品味，不如说取决于房价。

vocab.say: say less about magic than about how Icelanders treat their land

pick.q: The way people spend their weekends says ___ about their jobs than about their personality.
pick.why: 固定搭配 say less about A than about B；less 修饰的是“说明的程度”，不是可数名词，所以不用 fewer。

pick.q: Her choice of school says less about money ___ about what she wants to study.
pick.why: less ... than 是比较结构，前面用了 less，后面就接 than about B。

vocab.expr: Few A ..., yet surprisingly few B ...
vocab.conn: Few + 名词 + 动词 ..., yet surprisingly few + (will / do ...) + 相反的动作
vocab.zh: 很少有人……，可出人意料的是，也很少有人……（两头都不愿表态）
vocab.note: few 不带 a，意思是“很少、几乎没有”，语气偏否定（a few 才是“有几个”）。前半句说“很少人肯定 A”，按常理你会以为大多数人否定 A；yet surprisingly few 立刻反转：“出人意料的是，否定 A 的人也很少”。结论就是：大多数人站在中间，不肯定也不否定。yet = but，比 but 更书面、更有转折感。surprisingly 修饰 few，表示“少得出人意料”。

ex.en: Few people enjoy exams, yet [[surprisingly few]] want to get rid of them.
ex.zh: 很少有人喜欢考试，可出人意料的是，想取消考试的人也很少。

ex.en: Few of my friends say they love their jobs, yet [[surprisingly few]] are looking for new ones.
ex.zh: 我的朋友里很少有人说自己热爱工作，可出人意料的是，在找新工作的人也很少。

ex.en: Few tourists can name a single Icelandic writer, yet [[surprisingly few]] leave without buying a book.
ex.zh: 很少有游客能说出哪怕一位冰岛作家的名字，可出人意料的是，空手不买书就离开的人也很少。

vocab.say: Few Icelanders will swear that elves exist, yet surprisingly few will rule it out.

pick.q: ___ students like homework, yet surprisingly few want to stop doing it.
pick.why: 这里要的是“很少有学生喜欢作业”这个否定意思，用 Few；A few 是“有几个”，偏肯定，前后就不成对比了。

pick.q: Few people believe the story, ___ surprisingly few say it is false.
pick.why: 后半句和常理相反（你以为会有很多人说它是假的），是转折，用 yet；so 表示结果，意思不通。

breakdown.en: When machines break down or workers fall ill on a site, someone usually jokes that the elves are behind it, and only half of them are joking.
points: 句子由 when 从句 + 主句 + and 连接的第二个分句组成：什么时候 → 有人说什么 → 而且只有一半是开玩笑。
When machines break down or workers fall ill on a site：when 从句里有两个并列的情况，用 or 连接，on a site 是两件事共同的地点。
someone usually jokes that the elves are behind it：jokes 后面接 that 从句，说开玩笑的内容；be behind it = 是背后的原因。
and only half of them are joking：them 指说这话的人。字面是“只有一半在开玩笑”，言下之意是另一半是认真的，这是全句的笑点。
